newsitem.title: UK: ACPC technical meeting ends after number crunching.
newsitem.headline: ACPC technical meeting ends after number crunching.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries' (ACPC) technical group wrapped up a meeting on Friday with the group having prepared the ground for Saturday's Council meeting, delegates said.
"The ACPC's technical group looked at export figures...We have basically prepared the ground for tomorrow (Saturday)," said one ACPC delegate.
ACPC Secretary General Roberio Oliviera Silva said the meeting was a routine technical meeting with delegates discussing 1995/96 and 1996/97 export figures.
Oliviera said the ACPC on Saturday would also be reviewing the market situation.
The ACPC last met in May when it agreed a new plan to limit green coffee exports from its members to 53.5 million (60 kg) bags in the year to June 1997 against 45.8 million in the previous 12 months.
Preliminary ACPC figures show exports from the group in 1995-96 reached 47 million bags.
The ACPC's technical group is made up of representatives of El Salvador, Brazil, Ivory Coast, Colombia, Uganda and Indonesia.
Delegates on Friday said while the technical group meeting was over, informal producer talks will continue this afternoon.
